assertion: The FBI and the Environmental Protection Agency issued a warning in July that malicious cyber actors are targeting the water and wastewater sector.
measure: water system cyber attack programmable logic controller incidents
independent_value: FBI/EPA PSA I-073026-PSA dated 30 July 2026: actors targeting internet-facing Rockwell MicroLogix 1100/1400 PLCs; water utilities in at least seven states reported incidents since 27 July.

assertion: After remotely accessing internet-facing devices, the actors changed the IP addresses and passwords, resulting in a loss of monitoring and control functionality. To reduce the risk of compromise, the FBI and EPA recommend removing PLCs from direct internet exposure via secure gateway and firewalls, setting up strong, unique passwords, and utilizing an access control list (ACL)...
independent_value: Matches the PSA text nearly verbatim.

assertion: Of the 12 states said to be attacked, nine have publicly confirmed they were hit: Michigan, Minnesota, Georgia, New Jersey, South Dakota, Utah, Oregon, Arkansas, Alabama
measure: water system cyber attack incidents by state
reason: The FBI PSA says at least seven states; the 12 figure is press-reported. Minnesota (30+ systems) is confirmed by the IBTimes/WIRED report; Georgia and Michigan by search results. No page found confirming Utah, Oregon, Arkansas or Alabama.
why_no_page: Axios and CSIS returned 403; the IBTimes page that loaded covers Minnesota only.

reason: CSIS page returned 403 and the claim text was not read. Context against: the FBI/EPA PSA names no actor; IBTimes reports private firms still debating the group, with Tenable pointing to CyberAv3ngers and Claroty to Handala; an NPR piece reportedly says no group took credit.

assertion: In an interview Sunday on CNN, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton was asked by Dana Bash if Americans should stock up on water and other basic goods. Clayton largely avoided the question but said, "We have been living with interruptions,"
inaccuracy: The article places the exchange in a water-hack story; Reuters shows the interview was about a wave of tech outages (air travel, Microsoft, banks, NSA) that Clayton said were not coordinated or state-sponsored. The Bash stock-up question itself is not in the Reuters text.
independent_value: Reuters (Nov 22): Clayton on CNN State of the Union Sunday said 'glitches, gaps, interruptions in service' will happen; on ABC said outages were not coordinated or state-sponsored.

assertion: In a November 16 interview on Fox News, Vice President JD Vance said: "We do not see some crisis coming down, but you have to be prepared for everything."
independent_value: TheWrap quotes Vance on The Ingraham Angle Monday evening (Nov 16): 'We do not see some crisis coming down. But you have to be prepared for everything.' The question was about outages and stocking up, not water hacks.

assertion: The Trump administration has downplayed the warnings in part.
independent_value: Vance said there is no crisis coming; Clayton said outages are upgrade-related, not coordinated attacks. The administration also issued the water PSA.
